published.pgda69_note: PGDA product 69 (Mazarico et al. 2011 method, LDEM_75S_120M, 18.6-yr cycle): fraction of timesteps with ANY part of the disc visible. 'Ours' = our default (5 m + 120 m DEM, 2 m observer). 'Replication' = same 120 m DEM only, observer at the surface (0 m), any-part definition, evaluated at the nearest 120 m pixel centre with rays starting one pixel out, over 2009-01-01..2027-08-08 (one nodal cycle; PGDA's exact period is not stated). PGDA's own ray-tracing details differ, so this is an approximate replication.

connecting_ridge_breakdown.reading: Same DEM, same point: our method gives 75.2% Sun vs PGDA's 75.2%. The big change is the observer height: 55.1% at ground level vs 89.9% with a 2 m mast. At ground level the site point sits on a ~1.4° slope, and the Sun never rises more than ~1.5° here, so the ground just uphill blocks it; a 2 m mast clears that. Earth swings ±7° and barely changes (56-58%). At ground level, moving 55 m on the 120 m surface also changes the Sun value (75 -> 54%).
